prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1186; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision in Pasadena, Texas?

A: Yes, that's right. I was driving my car when it happened.

Q: Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road, waiting for the signal to change. Traffic was moderate, and I had my foot on the brake.

Q: Did you notice the other vehicle before it hit you?

A: Not really. I looked in my mirror a second before, but I didn't see it coming fast enough to react. The impact came from behind and pushed me forward into the car in front of me.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you feel any injuries at the scene?

A: I felt a sharp pain in my neck right away, and my lower back started to tighten within a few minutes. I didn't think much of it at first, but it got worse over the next day.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day, and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week since then. They diagnosed me with a neck and back strain.

Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limited movement?

A: Yes. Turning my head to the left is difficult, and sitting for more than about thirty minutes makes my back ache. I've been taking over-the-counter pain relievers and doing the exercises the therapist gave me.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to make sure my medical bills and time off work are taken into account.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.

A: Thank you.
